correctness.rationale: The theorem is mathematically correct. In the classical mixed-area identity the first polygon's normals have angles π/n+2πj/n and the common side length is 2R sin(π/n). At each normal the rotated second polygon contributes S times the cosine of the signed offset from the nearest vertex. Modulo 2π/m, the step 2π/n has order N=n/d and fills the grid of spacing 2δ with multiplicity d. Centering its representatives yields x+(2k−N+1)δ, k=0,…,N−1; the range is the reduced support interval with harmless endpoint ties. Summing the finite geometric series gives d sin(π/m) cos x/sin δ, hence the claimed area and exact extrema. In the proof at line 61, 'parallel' must mean coincident outward normals, not undirected parallelism (opposite normals can occur away from the minimum, e.g. triangles at θ=π). Directly the coincidence angles are θ≡π/n−π/m mod 2δ, the minimizing phase since Nδ=π/m. The two equally spaced normal sets then share exactly d directions, and polygon Minkowski addition takes the union of their normals, proving the stated side counts including aligned angles. For uniform rotation |x| is uniform on [0,δ], so the stated decreasing cosine pushforward, moments and normalized limit follow by integration and Taylor expansion. The local wording defect does not invalidate any final claim. No replacement is supplied because the result fails the originality/value checks.
